name: xdbml
__comment_top__: DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE DIRECTLY. Edit xdbml.tmLanguage.template.json and run tools/textmate/scripts/build.mjs. Placeholder strings (delimited by double underscores) are filled with case-insensitive regex alternations from parser/src/keywords.ts.

patterns.comment: Top-of-file version directive: `xdbml: 0.1` or `experimental: ...`. Recognized only at the start of a line with the colon immediately after, to avoid colliding with `xdbml` appearing elsewhere.

module-directives.comment: v0.2 module system (spec §26): `use` / `reuse ... from '...'` directives, plus the `as` alias keyword. Matched as standalone words anywhere; TextMate cannot disambiguate context cheaply, but these keywords are rare outside their proper position so false positives are minimal. The `as` keyword also serves DBML table-aliasing (`Table users as u`) for which the same scope is appropriate.

metadata-declaration.comment: A Metadata block (spec 24.7, v0.7): the keyword, the kind of element, and the target. Matched only as a whole, so an entity or a field may still be named metadata.

dep-declaration.comment: A Dep (spec 27.2, v0.7): the keyword at the start of a line, before ':', '{' or '[', or before a name and one of them. Indented in a body, or before a type, dep names an entity or a field.

change-blocks.comment: Change blocks (spec 29, v0.8). The words are colored only in the positions of a statement, so a field may still be named drop or modify (spec 29.3).

patterns.comment: Changes starts a change block (spec 29.1, v0.8) at the start of a line, before its name, its settings and '{'.
A statement (spec 29.3): create, alter or drop, then the kind of element, and if exists or if not exists.
An action of alter on a part (spec 29.7): add, modify, drop or rename, then Field, Column, Index, Constraint or Value.
modify on the element itself, before its settings, drop or source_query (spec 29.8). Before a type alone, modify is left uncolored, since a field may be named modify.
drop before the settings it removes (spec 29.8): a bracket, not null, primary key, or a setting name.

lineage-arrows.comment: The arrows of a dependency (spec 27, v0.7): -> from upstream to downstream, <- from downstream to upstream, in a Dep and in a dep setting.
lineage-arrows.name: keyword.operator.lineage.xdbml

declarations.comment: All declaration keywords. The keyword is followed by an identifier (the declared name). `Note` is skipped where it names a field (spec 3.10): it counts as a keyword only before ':' or '{', or before the name of a sticky note, qualified or not, its settings brackets, and '{' or ':' on the same line (spec 19.2).

type-keywords.comment: Structural type and polymorphism keywords (object, array, oneOf, etc.). Matched wherever they appear -- which in xDBML is always in a type position after a colon, but TextMate doesn't track context cheaply, so we accept them anywhere.

block-keywords.comment: Keywords that open a block in an entity body (indexes, checks, constraints, records). Matched only before '{', so a field may still carry one of these names; records also before the '(' of a column list or the '[' of its settings (spec 26.1, v0.7), which no field type starts with.
block-keywords.name: keyword.other.block.xdbml

diagram-view-categories.comment: The categories of a DiagramView body (Entities or Tables, Views, Containers or Schemas, EntityGroups or TableGroups, SupertypeGroups, Notes; spec 18.1). Matched only before '{', so an entity or a field may still carry one of these names.
diagram-view-categories.name: keyword.declaration.category.xdbml

native-types.comment: Target-native type names (Oracle number, PostgreSQL serial, ...), colored like scalar types. Highlighting only: any identifier is a valid type name.
native-types.name: storage.type.xdbml

x-properties.comment: Custom AI-readiness properties prefixed with `x_` or `x-`. Highlighted as extension points.
x-properties.name: support.other.x-property.xdbml

x-quoted-properties.comment: A quoted setting key with the `x-` prefix, "x-hackolade-id", is a custom property as an `x_` key is (spec 24.5, v0.7.1). Matched only before ':', ahead of the strings, which would read it as a quoted identifier.
x-quoted-properties.name: support.other.x-property.xdbml

settings-block.comment: Square-bracket settings block. Inside, we recognize flag settings, keyed settings, ordinary string/number values, and cardinality operators (>, <, -) for Ref-style settings.

setting-keys.comment: Setting keys appear before a colon. Matched only here inside the settings block.

cardinality-strings.comment: Cardinality settings have values like '0..*' or '1..1' that we color as a distinct kind of string.
cardinality-strings.name: string.unquoted.cardinality.xdbml

ref-cardinality-operators.comment: Cardinality operators (>, <, -, <>) in Ref declarations, with the '?' that marks an end optional (>?, ?<, ?-?; spec 11.1, v0.7). Recognized between two qualified identifiers (foo.bar >? baz.qux). The pattern requires word characters or dots on each side to avoid matching `>` in comments or other contexts.
ref-cardinality-operators.name: keyword.operator.cardinality.xdbml

patterns.comment: Triple-quoted multi-line string (DBML extension). Must come before single-quoted matcher.
patterns.name: string.quoted.triple.xdbml

patterns.comment: Double-quoted identifier (used to escape reserved keywords as names).
patterns.name: string.quoted.double.xdbml
